judged_text: The 'retrieved recently' redis marker is committed (setnx + expire) before perform_retrieve runs, so a failed retrieval leaves the marker in place for its full 60-second TTL. Every retry within the next 60 seconds — retries of the failed job and the loading page's 30-second re-enqueues — enters retrieve, sees the marker, and returns success without attempting the work, so the system reports success while the retrieval never happened; recovery depends entirely on the user keeping the page open past the throttle window.

Every retry within the next 60 seconds — retries of the failed job and the loading page's 30-second re-enqueues — enters retrieve, sees the marker, and returns success without attempting the work, so the system reports success while the retrieval never happened; recovery depends entirely on the user keeping the page open past the throttle window.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, the throttle marker is set via `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)` *before* `perform_retrieve` is called (`retrieve` does `perform_retrieve unless ... retrieved_recently?`). If `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http`/`TopicEmbed.import_remote` fails (network/readability/open errors, etc.) or returns without creating the embed, the redis key still remains for 60s, causing subsequent calls within that window to return early and skip retrieval. This interacts with `EmbedController#best` rendering `loading` (reloads every 30s) and enqueuing `Jobs::RetrieveTopic`, so repeated attempts can be suppressed by the throttle despite no embed being created.
